advisor.function.secdef_no_search_path.t: SECURITY DEFINER {kind, select, procedure {procedure} other {function}} {function} does not pin search_path
advisor.function.secdef_no_search_path.d: {function} in database {database} runs with the privileges of its owner, {superuser, select, true {superuser} other {role}} {owner}, but finds the tables, functions and operators its body names through the caller's search_path. A caller who can create objects in a schema on that path, or a temporary table, can make it use their objects with those privileges. {public, select, true {Every role can call it: PUBLIC has EXECUTE, as it does on any function by default.} other {Only the roles granted EXECUTE can call it.}}
advisor.function.secdef_no_search_path.r: ALTER {kind, select, procedure {PROCEDURE} other {FUNCTION}} {function} SET search_path = {schema}, pg_temp; with pg_temp last, and schema-qualify the objects its body uses.{public, select, true { Then REVOKE EXECUTE ON {kind, select, procedure {PROCEDURE} other {FUNCTION}} {function} FROM PUBLIC; and grant EXECUTE to the roles that need it.} other {}}
advisor.function.untracked.title: Function calls are not tracked in database {database}
advisor.function.untracked.detail: track_functions is none for the sessions of database {database}, so pg_stat_user_functions is empty: how often its {count, plural, one {# function} other {# functions}} in a procedural language (trigger functions among them) run, and how long they take, is unknown.
advisor.function.untracked.remediation: ALTER SYSTEM SET track_functions = 'pl'; SELECT pg_reload_conf(); or, for this database only, ALTER DATABASE {databaseIdent} SET track_functions = 'pl';. 'pl' costs little; 'all' also tracks SQL and C functions at a higher cost, and an SQL function the planner inlines is never tracked. pglens never changes the setting.
